title: Gingham Inn, Jean Calloway and re-forming the band for a tour
summary: After the Gingham Inn closes, owners bring in singer Jean Calloway; Hudson, Walter Page, Morty Long, Lester Nichols and Trombone Smitty join as the band tours.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: And we played out there about three weeks. And they closed the place down.
That was the Gingham Inn, wasn't it?

Gingham Inn, yes. We played about three and a half -- about three weeks. And they closed -- and the place closed down. So the owners decided to keep our band do -- together, they secured the services of a young lady named Jean Calloway. Jean Calloway had a nice voice and she could front a band. And back in those days the word Calloway was pretty hot. So, they sent for Jean Calloway to come to St. Louis. She came to St. Louis and we rehearsed and, in the meantime, we augmented the band by sending to Kansas City for George Hudson, to come to St. Louis and join the band. We sent George Hudson a bus ticket.

George came and joined the band. Mr. Pitts left the band, we sent and got Walter Page on bass. To join the band. Our piano player left the band, Mr. Goodman, -- Goodson, so we hired a piano player in St. Louis, by the name of --
Morty Long.
Morty Long. So we had -- we had Harry Edison on trumpet, George Hudson on trumpet, Snub Mosely left
the band, I'm trying to think whether he left the band before we started our tour -- I think he did, didn't he?
Uh-huh.
Snub Mosely left the band to join orchestra. So, we rehearsed the band, the drummer left too. A. G. Godley left and we hired Spare Ribs, what was his name?
Lester Nichols.
Lester Nichols, we hired a young man named Lester Nichols on the drums. I can't remember who we had on trombone or whether we had a trombone player or not. Can you remember, Charles?
I can't remember right now.
Right. Well anyway, we left on this tour and this tour tooks us to Kansas; Hayes, Kansas; we played all through Kansas, we played up in Missouri, we played --
Oklahoma City.
Oklahoma City, we played Mark Twain's home town, Hannibal, Missouri. We played across the river from Hannibal, in a place called Quincy, Illinois.
Trombone, Smitty.
That's right, Trombone Smitty. What was his name, Smitty?
Oh, my goodness.
(Unintelligible).
We hired a trombone player named Smitty.
He came to us, I think, from Indianapolis.
Uh-huh.

He was born in Evansville, Indiana. He was a genius on the trombone. And that was our brass section, George Hudson, Harry Edison, and Trombone Smitty, everybody called him Smitty. We toured all the hamlets in Missouri, Mexico, Missouri; Paris, Missouri; and southern Illinois, Oklahoma, --
